name: Rice-paper cheese bourekas — lean (cottage + 9% + light Bulgarian + parsley)

source.author: Lean, dual-lens-optimized version of rice_paper_cheese_bourekas
source.notes: Leaned-out version of the rice-paper cheese bourekas, designed with the user and adopted. Cheese blend swapped to cottage 5% + 9% yellow + light Bulgarian 5% (no full-fat yellow/mozzarella), with a generous amount of fresh parsley folded in for folate/iron/vitamin C. Baked, not fried. Makes ~10; macros PER BOUREKA. Parsley taken at ~60 g ('a nice amount' — exact amount flexible, barely moves macros). No added salt (the Bulgarian salts it). Estimate.

ingredients.note: dipped a few seconds, not soaked
high protein, lower fat than full-fat yellow
salty — no added salt needed; verify pasteurized (her note)
folate + iron + vitamin C; amount flexible
no added salt — Bulgarian covers it

steps: Mix the filling (cottage, grated 9% yellow, crumbled light Bulgarian, chopped parsley, 1 egg, pepper) to a uniform mix. No added salt — the Bulgarian is salty.
In a shallow plate mix the dip: 1 egg + ½ tbsp honey + a little water.
Dip one rice paper a few seconds until slightly pliable (not fully soft).
Lay it flat, put ~1 tbsp filling in the center and fold into a rectangle (envelope).
Place on greased parchment, folds facing UP.
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle sesame + nigella.
Bake 220 °C ~25 min until deep golden and crispy.

batch_totals.note: ~10 bourekas. Vs the original (per boureka ~127 kcal / 6.4 g protein / 6.3 g fat): MORE protein (7.6 g), ~40% less fat (3.9 g), lower sodium — because cottage + 9% yellow + light Bulgarian replace the full-fat cheeses, plus generous parsley for folate/iron. Baked, no frying.

him.verdict: The lean version is a genuinely great high-protein snack: ~7.6 g protein for ~110 kcal per boureka (~6.9 g protein per 100 kcal) with only ~3.9 g fat, baked (no frying), in a light rice-paper wrapper. Swapping the full-fat cheeses for cottage + 9% yellow + LIGHT Bulgarian is what did it — more protein, far less fat than the original, and the generous parsley adds a little folate and fiber. Low-sodium-ish for a cheese pastry (~195 mg). Excellent for portion control — log by the piece.
flags: ~7.6 g protein / 110 kcal (~6.9 g protein per 100 kcal)
only ~3.9 g fat/boureka — ~40% less than the original

suggested_mods: Great as-is; 2–3 bourekas is a solid high-protein snack
Push parsley toward a full cup for even more folate/fiber
Serve with tomato/pepper for vitamin C

her_preconception.verdict: A solid preconception snack now — fully baked (egg filling + wash cooked through), with calcium + protein from the cheeses, choline from the eggs, and a real folate/iron/vitamin-C lift from the generous parsley (vitamin C aids iron absorption). The one flag is the light Bulgarian — a brined soft cheese: it's baked through here (cooked = considered safe) and light Israeli Bulgarit is usually pasteurized, but verify it. Dropping the full-fat cheeses also makes it lighter overall.
prenatal_highlights: folate + iron + vitamin C from generous parsley
fully baked; lighter and lower-fat than the original

safety_advisories.note: Light Bulgarian is a brined soft cheese — verify pasteurized. It's baked through here (considered safe cooked).
safety_advisories.swap: verify pasteurized / keep baked through, or shift to more cottage + 9% yellow

suggested_mods: A full cup of parsley pushes folate higher
Serve with tomato/pepper for extra vitamin C

adopted_note: Adopted 2026-10-08 as the lean version of the rice-paper cheese bourekas (supersedes rice_paper_cheese_bourekas for actual use). Per boureka (of ~10, ~50 g): ~110 kcal, 7.6 g protein, 3.9 g fat, ~195 mg sodium. him 9 / her 8. Standing spec: filling = 150 g cottage 5% + 120 g of 9% yellow + 75 g light Bulgarian 5% + a generous ~60 g parsley + 1 egg, no added salt; dip = egg + ½ tbsp honey + water; bake 220 C ~25 min, folds up. Verify Bulgarian pasteurized; parsley amount flexible (more = more folate).
cooking_guide: Mix the filling: cottage, grated 9% yellow, crumbled light Bulgarian, the chopped parsley, 1 egg and pepper, to a uniform mix. Taste — you shouldn't need added salt, the Bulgarian salts it.
Make the dip in a shallow plate: 1 egg + ½ tbsp honey + a little water, whisked. The egg-honey wash is the crunch secret and helps browning.
Dip ONE rice paper for just a few seconds — until slightly pliable, not fully soft. Over-dipping makes it tear and go gummy.
Lay it flat, put ~1 tbsp filling in the center (don't overfill) and fold into a rectangle like an envelope.
Place on greased parchment with the FOLDS FACING UP — keeps the base flat and the whole thing crisp.
Brush each with beaten egg and sprinkle sesame + nigella.
Bake at 220 °C (or Ninja Grill on Bake) ~25 min until deep golden and very crispy. Watch the last few minutes — rice paper crisps fast.
Tips: a full cup of parsley adds more folate/fiber; a grating of garlic or chili flakes lifts the filling; serve with tomato/pepper for vitamin C.
